notes: An FPS with a free-for-all answer is Shooter on the Arena Deathmatch preset, the one competitive row that does not assume two teams. I substituted the preset's lane-network for open-battlefield and kept its options: the answers describe an original hood neighbourhood of about four city blocks with its own streets, buildings and landmarks, which is one contiguous map of dispersed points of interest rather than parallel lanes feeding a front, and open-battlefield costs the same P0. cover-los covers the street furniture and corners a small map needs, path-loop keeps the blocks interconnected the way arcade shooters want, and settlement-density carries the four-block neighbourhood grid itself; that count of four blocks is recorded here since the form has no count field. Without a user I read the loading screen and the main hub with its play button as UI rather than a place to build, which is why there is no portal hub and no separate lobby map, and I left buildings as facades since nothing says players go inside, keeping this off the not-yet-ready interior transition pass.
